newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta, Saskatchewan face frost risk Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Alberta, Saskatchewan face frost risk Tuesday.

text.p: Alberta and Saskatchewan's grain growing regions on Monday were forecast to face a slight to high risk of overnight frost Tuesday morning, Environment Canada said.
A high risk of frost was forecast for Alberta's Peace River Valley, Environment Canada's 10-day frost outlook said.
A moderate risk was forecast for Alberta and Saskatchewan's northern grainbelt while a slight risk was forecast for the central and southern grainbelts of both provinces.
No risk was forecast for Manitoba Tuesday morning.
A slight risk of frost was forecast for eastern Saskatchewan and west and central Manitoba Wednesday morning.
A moderate risk was forecast for southeastern Manitoba Wednesday morning.
There was no risk of frost seen anywhere on the Prairie grainbelt Thursday morning.
A slight risk of frist was forecast for Alberta's Peace River Valley and westcentral Alberta's grainbelt Friday and Saturday mornings.
A slight risk of frost was forecast for the south, central and northern Alberta grainbelt Sept 16 to 18.
